questions.def: Future perfect indicates completion before a future point.
questions.question: By the time he arrives, we ___ dinner.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for an action started and continuing.
questions.question: She ___ her research for three years now.

questions.def: Use 'arrives' only for present simple, but here we need present perfect ('has arrived').
questions.question: By the time he arrives, I will be finished writing the report.

questions.def: Past perfect indicates an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ in Paris before moving to Rome.

questions.def: 'Was supposed' expresses unfulfilled past intention.
questions.question: He ___ to call, but he forgot.

questions.def: Future perfect: completed action before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, she ___ her degree.

questions.def: Stative verbs ('know') are not typically used in continuous tenses.
questions.question: She is knowing the answer but won't tell.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in past, continuing.
questions.question: I ___ on this project for months, but I'm nearly done.

questions.def: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past.
questions.question: I wish I ___ harder in school.

questions.def: 'Had barely' implies that the action was nearly not completed.
questions.question: He ___ finished the report when I arrived.

questions.def: Use 'had started' (past perfect) for action before 'got'.
questions.question: By the time we got there, the movie was already started.

questions.def: 'Were' is the subjunctive form used in conditional sentences.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.

questions.def: 'Is rumored' is a passive form expressing a popular belief.
questions.question: He ___ to have been a spy.

questions.def: 'Am going to' expresses a future plan or intention.
questions.question: I ___ to see him tomorrow.

questions.def: Stative verbs like 'know' are not typically continuous.
questions.question: She has been knowing him for many years.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous emphasizes duration before future time.
questions.question: By next summer, I ___ English for five years.

questions.def: 'Hardly had' introduces an inverted sentence structure.
questions.question: Hardly ___ he entered the room when the phone rang.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for ongoing action since past.
questions.question: She ___ the piano since she was a child.

questions.def: 'Know' is a stative verb and not typically continuous.
questions.question: I have been knowing about this for ages.

questions.def: Past perfect: completion before a past point in time.
questions.question: He ___ the work before the deadline.

questions.def: 'Scarcely had' introduces an inverted sentence structure.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ I arrived than it started to rain.

questions.def: 'Was supposed to' indicates unfulfilled past intention.
questions.question: He ___ to the meeting yesterday.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had' needed for action completed before 'arrived'.
questions.question: By the time I arrived, they have already left.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in past, continues.
questions.question: I ___ for you for over an hour.

questions.def: 'No sooner had' introduces an inverted sentence structure.
questions.question: No sooner ___ I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before a future time.
questions.question: She ___ the report by the end of the week.

questions.def: 'Know' is stative, use 'have known' with 'since' to express a state over time.
questions.question: I have been knowing him since 2010.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in past, continues.
questions.question: They ___ in this city for ten years now.

questions.def: 'As if' uses the past subjunctive for unreal situations.
questions.question: He acted as if he ___ everything.

questions.def: Present perfect indicates a state lasting since the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since we were in college.
